questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Exploring Spain and going surfing.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Surf opportunities and the language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The local volunteer students did an outstanding job with helping and organizing trips, parties and events. Probably one of the better Erasmus student networks of Europe. :)

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Once you get into the Whatsapp groups and Facebook groups of the Erasmus student network, it was very easy to find information. Getting into the groups can be a little bit tricky, but searching for ESN Oviedo in Facebook is would be my best advice.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
In the Whatsapp groups you can get in contact with a local student who can answer most of your questions. 
Sorting everything out with the host institution and hospital is way more tricky, especially with the learning agreement.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
Sorting everything out with the host institution and hospital is tricky, especially with the learning agreement. 
The e-mail contact with the host university and hospital is also not optimal due to language issues and it feels like you are the first danish erasmus student that they receive.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Idealista, the Erasmus Whatsapp groups + Facebook group.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Most people find living through Idealista and you have to be lucky with your roomates. Living off campus is what everybody does, since people want to live in the city of Gijon/Oviedo.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Get in the Whatsapp groups, and try to find former student's places! There are a lot of opportunities, so you will always end up finding something.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Picking my courses/hospital departments was very confusing and tricky. If you're having a lot of problems, try to contact your danish supervisor and ask for help from one of the former Erasmus students that went to Oviedo/Gijon.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Get started in time, so you don't miss the different deadlines. So always keep a close eye to your e-mails and the mobility online form.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I got help from my danish supervisor and a former Erasmus student that was currently in Gijon/Oviedo. That way I managed to get the contact details of my host university/hospital.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end I got all the Departments that I wanted. Just not in the order i had wished.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Describe what you want or need, as if the host university never has had an Erasmus student from Denmark before. So be specific.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The more Spanish you speak the better. Most people understand a little bit of English, but they won't explain much if they can't explain in Spanish to you.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was Clinical rotations.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In Denmark they hospital departments are more prepared and demanding. So you learn a lot more in Denmark.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Emergency department, radiology, orthopaedic surgery and anestesiology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Emergency department and orthopaedic surgery.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Car parking was a problem in the city center of Gijon. You end up paying 375 kr/month. And parking tickets are very expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Car parking was more expensive than expected. Alcohol was less expensive than expected because of the deals that the locar erasmus student network provides you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great surfing conditions, skiing is possible in the winter. Hiking, beaches, sports, mountains.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: An Erasmus party 3x/week. Erasmus sports once a week. And then one day trip/week. On top of that weekend trips to Portugal, Sevilla, San Sebastian and Bilbao.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go All-in on the introduction weeks. And after that join whatever you like the most.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the nature of Asturias and the north of Spain.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the Tapas events which often end up in a party.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not so many vegetarian options.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The outgoing and open culture of the people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get into the Whatsapp groups as soon as possible. Join the introduction weeks. Get help from former Erasmus students for the Learning agreement.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Already given above.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The poeple that I met and the surfing.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding good roomates.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you like to surf, try to end up in Gijon. And if you have the possibility bring a car. That way you can easily get to the beaches even if you end up in Oviedo.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
